account:
Today’s ordinary business has been oddly thin: the scheduled council letters never arrived, and the grain inspection established only observed mill stock, not delivery terms. Meanwhile, several people are involved in preparations for the six o’clock great hall lighting inspection. Builder arranged it through an authorized appointment addendum, neighbour says the lighting looks splendid, and secretary will escort me. Builder specifically asked us not to enter before six. I am waiting outside with secretary and neighbour now, just before the appointed time.

What makes this unusual is the bread and the coordination around the hall. Baker had an order from freight for two hundred loaves; neighbour now reports builder saying two hundred fresh loaves are ready. Secretary has seen bread baked yesterday in two hall chests. Neighbour returned for the inspection, and secretary says innkeeper confirmed my six o’clock escort. Taken together, this could be preparation for a gathering or surprise involving food, with the lighting inspection serving as the reason to bring me into the hall. That is only my suspicion; nobody has told me there is a celebration or other concealed event.

There are also unresolved financial questions. Neighbour said innkeeper wanted to speak to me about an account and a spoiled batch. I heard baker nearby asking innkeeper who owes whom a separate thirty-emerald repayment, explicitly distinguishing it from the bread and grain account. I asked for details but have not received an explanation. Secretary has no definite knowledge of that repayment and no evidence that the hall bread is spoiled. Neighbour could not find innkeeper at the inn.

Finally, townspeople have repeated an oddly phrased rumour about a bridge or port change at the bakery, naming baker and neighbour. Neighbour cannot substantiate it and attributes it to Townsfolk thirteen. I have no direct evidence of any actual change. I should not confuse that gossip, the account dispute, and the hall preparations without further evidence.
